summary: Read-only study: NVDL/NVDX exit timing (pre-market vs 09:31) and entry timing (15:52 vs alternatives), each adversarially verified

study.summary: Keep the 09:31:05 exit. No candidate exit time beats it on average once spreads are counted, and the 'fade' the agent has seen live is a feature of the last ~6 weeks only. Data: Robinhood keeps 5-minute bars back to 2026-02-23 and 1-minute bars back to 2026-09-08. Earlier requests return only interpolated bars, so the requested 6-12 months became about 8 months. Tier A uses 5-minute extended bars over 164 non-earnings mornings (2026-02-23..10-20). Over that sample, selling pre-market at 08:00/09:00/09:15/09:25/09:29:59 averaged -0.9 to -7.6 bp vs the 09:31:05 proxy before costs (NVDL; t -0.4 to -1.3; NVDX the same). The 09:30 open print was -0.6 bp. The later times were: 09:35 +1.6 bp (t 0.2), 09:45 -8.1 bp, 10:00 -7.4 bp. Pre-market bids sit about 8 bp (NVDL) and about 9-27 bp (NVDX) under the trade prints, while our live 09:31 fills land on the 09:31 1-minute OHLC4 (+0.3 bp, n=24). Net of that, a pre-market exit loses about 10-13 bp a night on the position (about -$0.09 to -$0.11 a night). Tier B uses exact 1-minute data over the last 31 mornings (09-08..10-20). There, pre-market and the open print beat 09:31 by +21 to +28 bp gross (best t=1.9) because prices dropped in the first minute after the open; net that is about +15 bp, or +$0.12-0.14 a night. That drop is absent from the 133 earlier mornings (open to 09:35 averaged +7 bp; by month it ranged -64 to +30 bp). I also tested the conditional idea 'if the pre-market gap-up is large, sell at 09:25'. In-sample (Feb-Jul, 109 mornings) big gaps did reverse (+5.9 bp per 1% gap, t 2.1), but the rule picked there (gap > 1%) lost -35 bp per triggered night out of sample (Aug-Oct, n=25, t -2.9). Out of sample, gaps kept going in the same direction instead. So there is no robust gap rule. Both ETFs are approved for extended-hours trading (all_day_tradability tradable) and depth is no problem for 3 shares. The pre-market spread is the cost, and NVDX trades in only 42-61% of pre-market minutes.

sample.excluded: Mornings after NVDA earnings (Robinhood earnings calendar: NVDA reported 2026-02-25 pm, 05-20 pm, 08-26 pm), so exits on 2026-02-26, 2026-05-21 and 2026-08-27 were dropped (167 -> 164 mornings). Tier B (1-minute) = 31 mornings 2026-09-08..2026-10-20, no earnings inside. 2026-10-21 was used only to calibrate against the live fill. Gaps: Robinhood returns only interpolated bars for 5-minute data before 2026-02-23 and 1-minute data before about 2026-09-08 (checked on 2025-10/11, 2026-01-15, 02-17, 09-01). The full 6-12 month window was not available; 164 days meets the >=120 floor for 5-minute data only.

study.recommendation: Keep the 09:31:05 marketable-limit exit unchanged (RULES_v3 §5). Do not adopt a routine pre-market exit (extended_hours limit sell at 08:00-09:29), an exit on the 09:30 open print, a later regular-session exit (09:33-10:00), or a gap-conditional 'sell pre-market if gap > X%' rule. Reasons: (1) Over 164 mornings, pre-market prints averaged 1-8 bp below the 09:31 proxy before costs. Pre-market bids cost about another 8 bp (NVDL) and 9-27 bp (NVDX), so a pre-market exit expects to lose about 10-13 bp a night on the position, about -$0.09 to -$0.11 a night at about $85. (2) Later regular-session exits show nothing beyond noise (09:35 +2 bp, t 0.25; 09:45 and 10:00 -7 to -8 bp with 2-3x the variance). (3) The live opening fades are real for Sep-Oct 2026: open to 09:31 averaged -21 bp over 31 mornings, t 1.75. The previous 133 mornings did not show it (open to 09:35 +7 bp), and by month that drift swings between -64 and +30 bp. (4) An in-sample gap rule reversed out of sample (OOS -35 bp per triggered night, t -2.9). This matches §3(g): no rule changes on short windows. Two optional, low-cost items (no change to timing): (a) Shadow-log the NVDL/NVDX bid AND ask at 09:25 and 09:29 every exit morning, with no orders. That builds a real pre-market spread record so the study can be re-run on 1-minute data at the pre-registered ~40-night review (mid-December) or once there are 120 or more 1-minute mornings. (b) A marketable sell limit fills at the best bid anyway, so the first limit's buffer is a cap, not a cost. Widening the first cap (e.g. bid - 0.5%) and re-quoting immediately before sending would have avoided the 10/19 rest-then-re-price episode (about -80 bp, about $0.69 that night). That is worth about +$0.01-0.03 a night amortized, but it rests on a single event (low confidence).
study.spreads_bp: No historical quotes are available, so these are estimates, each labeled with its source. PRE-MARKET: journal bids compared with trade prints in the same +-2 minutes give an implied half-spread. NVDL: median 8.0 bp (mean 8.9, n=12) at 07:47-08:00 and median 6.6 bp (n=10, noisy, some '~' bids) at 09:00-09:16. NVDX: median 26.8 bp (n=5) at 07:47-08:00 and median 9.0 bp (n=7) at 09:00-09:16. 1-minute Roll full-spread estimates are rough: NVDL 4-9 bp pre-market; NVDX 0-10 bp (unreliable). NVDX trades in only 40-61% of pre-market minutes (median about 400-700 shares/minute), against 65-83% for NVDL (about 700-1100 shares/minute). At the open (09:30-09:34) Roll gives NVDL 29 bp and NVDX 27 bp full, but that figure includes volatility. Volume at the open is about 59k shares/minute (NVDL) and 12k (NVDX). Later Roll readings: 09:35-09:59 about 12-13 bp, 10:00-10:29 about 7 bp. Live quotes today at 09:49/09:59 ET: NVDL 33.79/33.80 and 33.95/33.96 (1 cent, ~3 bp); NVDX 19.00/19.01 and 19.09/19.10 (1 cent, ~5 bp). OUR COSTS: the 09:31 exit fill vs the 09:31 1-minute OHLC4 is NVDL +0.3 bp (n=24) and NVDX +8.6 bp (n=11). Fill vs the bid inferred from the order limit is NVDL -1.2 bp and NVDX +0.5 bp, so we sell at about the bid. The limit buffer is not paid. The 15:52 entry fill vs the 15:52 OHLC4 is NVDL -0.3 bp and NVDX -1.1 bp (sd 7). Cost model used for net figures: pre-market +8 bp NVDL, +25 bp NVDX before 09:00 and +12 bp from 09:00 to 09:29; open print +7 bp (uncertain); 09:33 and later 0 bp. At $85 (2 NVDL + 1 NVDX), 10 bp is about $0.085 a night.
study.live_calibration: The 09:31 1-minute OHLC4 tracks our real exit fills: NVDL mean +0.3 bp, median +4.5, sd 30, n=24 exits (2026-09-10..10-21); NVDX +8.6 bp, median +6.3, sd 37, n=11. Most of the scatter comes from timing within the minute (orders went out at 09:31:08-13). The bid inferred at about 09:31:05 sits 4-8 bp above the minute OHLC4, because prices kept falling within 09:31 in the recent window (09:31 close was about 4-6 bp under the OHLC4). The worst case was 10/19, when the first limits went stale and rested, then were re-priced at 60 s: -82 bp NVDL and -79 bp NVDX vs the OHLC4, about -$0.69. The best case was 10/15: +71 bp. The 10/21 exit (outside the sample) was NVDL +5 bp and NVDX -0.5 bp. 15:52 entries fill within about 1 bp of the 15:52 OHLC4. The 5-minute and 1-minute data match exactly on the 31 overlapping mornings. The 5-minute-based 09:31:05 proxy (open + 0.22*(close - open)) carried a +17 bp bias (RMSE 56 bp) in the recent window. Tier A conclusions change by less than 2 bp across the reference choices: open print, variance-weighted bridge w=0.44, or 5-minute OHLC4.
caveats: Data history is short: 5-minute bars start 2026-02-23 and 1-minute bars about 2026-09-08 (Robinhood returns only interpolated bars before that). The long sample is 164 mornings at 5-minute resolution. Exact 09:31 data covers only 31 mornings, all inside the most recent regime.

Tier A cannot observe 09:31:05. It uses a Brownian-bridge interpolation inside the 09:30-09:35 bar, which was biased +17 bp (RMSE 56) on the Tier B window. The conclusions hold with the open print and with 09:35 as references, but sub-5-minute structure before September is unknown.

Pre-market price = last trade at or before T. NVDX is thin pre-market (trades in 42-61% of minutes; last trade up to 10-23 minutes old on a few days). Historical bids/asks are unavailable. The pre-market spread estimate rests on 22 NVDL and 12 NVDX journal bids (some approximate '~'), with no asks.

Net t-stats for pre-market exits in Tier A (-2 to -4) mostly reflect the cost subtracted; gross differences are statistically zero (|t| <= 1.3). The conclusion is 'no gain, plus a cost', not 'a significant loss'.

Multiple comparisons: about 200 tests across 10 times x 3 references x 2 symbols x 2 tiers x 6 gap buckets x IS/OOS x 8 thresholds. The best pre-market result (t 1.9, Tier B) would not survive any correction. NVDL and NVDX correlate 0.97-0.99 per day, so NVDX is not independent confirmation.

Regime instability: open-to-09:35 drift by month ranged from -64 to +30 bp. Sep-Oct 2026 shows a real first-minute drop (open to 09:31 -21 bp, t 1.75; October -49 bp open to 09:35). If it persists, a pre-market exit would gain about +$0.12-0.14 a night. The longer sample says it usually does not persist.

Gap-conditional results flip sign between IS (mean reversion, slope +5.9 bp per 1%, t 2.1) and OOS (continuation, slope -10.7, t -2.2). Any threshold rule is data-mined. OOS buckets are small (gap<-2%: n=8).
The 09:30 open print is a theoretical candidate. Retail Robinhood orders queued for the open are not guaranteed the opening-cross price, and first-minute effective spreads are about 25-30 bp (Roll).

Tradability verified read-only on ****8334: NVDL and NVDX have all_day_tradability = tradable (extended-hours and all-day limit orders allowed) and extended_hours_fractional = false (whole shares are fine). I did not verify Robinhood's exact pre-market session start time with a tool. A pre-market sell of shares bought the previous afternoon is not a day trade.

Prices are split-adjusted (NVDL shows fractional adjusted prices early in 2026). Within-morning ratios are unaffected. Gap buckets use the prior official daily close and are unadjusted for distributions; no NVDL/NVDX ex-date fell on a sampled morning as far as the per-day NVDL-NVDX consistency check shows.

Several files (basket_usd.py, entry_timing.py, raw1/raw5, verify_entry/, daily.json at the top level) appeared in the scratch dir from a sibling workflow agent. I did not touch them, and my inputs were verified unchanged.

issues: Headline numbers reproduce. I pulled fresh Robinhood bars myself (5-minute extended 2026-02-23..10-20, 1-minute extended 2026-09-08..10-21, daily bars, and NVDA earnings via get_earnings_results), converted UTC to ET with zoneinfo, and dropped interpolated bars. All 167 days have a 09:30 'reg' bar and no session label disagrees with the ET clock, so there is no DST or bar-start error. Sample: 164 mornings in Tier A and 31 in Tier B after removing the 02-26, 05-21 and 08-27 exits (NVDA reported 02-25, 05-20 and 08-26 after the close, confirmed). Tier A results (09:25, 09:29:59, open, 09:35 and 08:00 vs the 09:31:05 proxy) and Tier B results (09:29 close and open vs the 09:31 OHLC4) match the study to 0.1 bp.

Data limits confirmed. 1-minute bars before 2026-09-08 and 5-minute bars before 2026-02-23 come back interpolated: I checked 08-04, 09-01, 09-02..04 and 02-20, in both 'regular' and 'extended', and 30-second bars too. 15-second bars exist only from about 2026-10-14, so there is no longer exact sample.

Tier A holds under every reference I tried. NVDL 09:25 vs reference, gross: bridge -4.4 (t -0.81), 09:30 open -3.8, (o+c)/2 -5.1, 5-minute OHLC4 -2.5, 09:35 -6.0. All |t| are below 1.4 and Wilcoxon p is above 0.15.

The main loophole I tested was whether the 5-minute proxy hides a first-minute drop in earlier months. It does not change the answer. In Tier B the open-to-09:31:05 drop (-20 bp) carried through to 09:35 (-19 bp; slope 1.06, corr 0.56), so a drop like that would show in 5-minute bars. Before Sep 8 (n=133), open to 09:35 was +7.2 bp. Pre-market still lost even under the worst-case assumption that the whole open-to-09:35 move happened in the first minute: 09:25 vs 09:35 -12.3 bp, 09:29:59 vs 09:35 -8.5 bp.

Tier B with my own references is a bit stronger than the study says, but it is entirely an October effect. NVDL 09:29 close vs a 09:31:05 bridge (o31 + 5/60*(c31 - o31)) is +24.0 bp (t 2.10, Wilcoxon p 0.06, bootstrap 95% CI +1.7..+45.7). Against the 09:31 open it is +23.6 (t 2.10), and the open print is +20.1 (t 2.02). Split by month: September (n=17) +5.2 bp, October (n=14) +46.9 bp. Nominal p 0.044 becomes about 0.44 after a Bonferroni correction for about 10 candidate times, and NVDX (corr about 0.98) is not independent confirmation.

Overstated claim: the gap-rule out-of-sample failure. The study's -34.6 bp net (t -2.88, n=25) uses the 5-minute bridge proxy, which reads 16-17 bp too high in Sep-Oct. On the 15 out-of-sample trigger days that have exact 1-minute data (Sep 8+), the IS-chosen rule (gap > 1%, sell at 09:25) made +8.7 bp net (t 0.39). Gross it was +16.7 vs 09:31:05, against -4.0 with the proxy on the same days. The out-of-sample loss rests on 10 August mornings: -60 bp vs the proxy and -50 vs the open, so it does hold across references there. The conclusion 'no robust gap rule' still stands (the sign flips between periods), but 'fails out of sample at t -2.9' overstates the evidence.

Undercount of re-prices in the live calibration. The study's s05_live.py reads order times only from key 't', but the 86 orders.jsonl records before about 09-21 use 'ts'. So it missed the 2026-09-14 exit, where the first limit was 31.40 against a 31.45 bid, it rested, was re-priced and filled at 31.2101 (-59 bp vs the 09:31:05 bridge). That makes 2 rest-and-re-price exits in 24 NVDL exits, not 1. The other is 10/19 at -115 bp vs 09:31:05 (the study says -82 vs OHLC4). Amortized that is about -7 bp a night (about $0.06), not $0.01-0.03. It strengthens item (b) somewhat but is still only 2 events.

Live counterfactual is inconclusive. Selling at the 09:29 pre-market print minus 8 bp, compared with our actual fills: NVDL +17.7 bp (t 0.99, n=24); +10.1 without the 10/19 re-price. NVDX -19.0 bp (n=11).

Spread costs are roughly right but rest on thin evidence. My estimate is the journal bid vs the last 1-minute print at or before the same minute. NVDL: median 9.8 bp before 09:00 (n=12) and 6.0 bp from 09:00 to 09:16 (n=11, range -42 to +28, noisy). NVDX: 14.8 bp (n=7) and 12.6 bp (n=10). Every observation comes from 10/08-10/21 and none from 09:25-09:29. The study's 8 bp NVDL / 12 bp NVDX cost model is plausible to within about 5 bp. That does not decide anything: Tier A gross is about 0, and Tier B gross (+24) exceeds any plausible cost.

Minor issues. (a) The month range for open to 09:35 includes Feb 2026 with n=4, so the extreme monthly figure (+64 / -64 bp depending on sign) comes from 4 mornings. (b) The study's 09:45/10:00 figures use the 09:40/09:55 bar closes; using the 09:45/10:00 bar opens gives -7.5 and -8.5 bp, close to its -8.1 and -7.4. (c) Live orders were sent at 09:31:08-14, not 09:31:05, so on fast mornings the 'bid at 09:31:05' is already stale.

No problems with survivorship, look-ahead or overlap. The gap uses the 09:25 price and the prior official close; the official close matches the prior day's 15:55 5-minute close (median 0 bp; worst case 60 bp on NVDL 02-27). Mornings do not overlap, and the IS/OOS split is chronological. The multiple-comparison risk is real and the study acknowledges it.

Verifier files (not an issue): scripts /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/exec_timing/verify_exit/v01_load.py, v02_tables.py, v03_stats.py, v04_gap.py, v05_live.py, v06_tierB_robust.py, v07_spread.py; outputs v03_out.txt, v04_out.txt, v05_out.txt, v06_out.txt, v07_out.txt, vA.csv, vB.csv, bars.pkl; raw data in raw1/, raw5/, rawday/ (all under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/exec_timing/verify_exit/). Everything was read-only: no files under /home/user/test-trading were modified and no order, watchlist or alert tools were called.
verdict.adjusted_recommendation:
Adopt the core recommendation: keep the 09:31:05 marketable-limit exit, and adopt no pre-market, open-print, later (09:33-10:00) or gap-conditional exit. Over 164 mornings, pre-market is about equal to 09:31 before costs under every reference, including the worst case for the earlier months, and costs another 6-15 bp in spread. The recent advantage (+24 bp gross, t 2.1) comes from 14 October mornings (Sep +5, Oct +47) and does not survive a multiple-comparison correction.

Adopt the shadow log now, since it costs nothing. Each exit morning, record NVDL and NVDX bid and ask, with timestamps, at 09:25, 09:29 and 09:31:05, plus the fill time and price. Stop citing the gap-rule out-of-sample t of -2.9 as strong evidence. The honest statement is 'sign unstable across subperiods; the exact data on Sep-Oct triggers was +9 bp net, n=15'.

Defer item (b), widening the first exit cap, to the pre-registered 40-night review (mid-December). It now has 2 events (9/14 and 10/19, about -7 bp a night amortized, about $0.06), not 1, but n=2 is still anecdotal. Re-quote right before sending, since orders currently go out at 09:31:08-14.

Fix the review test in advance so it cannot be data-mined. At the review, switch to a pre-market (09:29) exit only if the fresh nights after 10/21 show a mean of shadow-logged 09:29 bid minus the actual 09:31 fill of at least +10 bp with t of at least 2. Otherwise keep 09:31:05. Re-run the timing study once there are 120 or more 1-minute mornings (about March 2027). Expected gain of any timing change today: $0 a night.
verdict.confidence: Medium-high that no exit-timing change should be made now. All headline numbers reproduce exactly, and the conclusion holds across 5 reference choices and the worst-case intra-bar path. Low confidence in any statement about sub-5-minute behaviour before September (it cannot be observed) and in the size of the pre-market spread (about 40 journal bids, all from Oct 8-21, none at 09:25-09:29).

study.summary:
15:52 is not measurably worse than any entry time we can actually use between 15:30 and 16:15. I tested every candidate time against the 15:52 reference on 164 NVDA-2x nights from 2026-02-23 to 2026-10-20 (5-minute bars, NVDA earnings nights excluded). Each one is within ±5bp of 15:52, and none has |t| above 1. Results for NVDL, in bp (negative means a cheaper entry): 15:30 +3.9 (t 0.81), 15:45 -0.4, 15:50 +2.1, 15:55 -1.2, 15:59 last trade -2.5 (t -0.48), official close -1.6 (t -0.32), 16:01 -3.6, 16:05 -4.3 (t -0.72), 16:15 -4.2. NVDX looks the same, at +4.1 to -5.3bp, all |t| below 0.9.

The in-sample (Feb to Jul, n=109) and out-of-sample (Aug to Oct, n=55) halves disagree:
- **In-sample:** later entries were not cheaper (close +0.8, 16:05 -2.2).
- **Out-of-sample:** later entries were cheaper by 4 to 9bp (15:55 -4.4 with t -1.54; close -6.4 with t -0.96).

Neither half is significant, and they do not agree with each other. The exact 1-minute data (31 nights, Sep 8 to Oct 20) agrees with the 5-minute proxies: correlation 0.94 to 0.97 for the late candidates, with a level offset of about 3bp. On those 31 nights the late entries are about 5 to 7bp cheaper, still with t about -0.5.

**Last 8 minutes (15:52 to 16:00):** the price does not move consistently up or down. NVDL averages -1.6bp (median +5.8, 90% bootstrap CI -9.9 to +6.3); NVDX averages -4.3bp (t -0.82). I also tested one specific idea, that leveraged-ETF rebalancing pushes prices in the day's direction into the close. In-sample it looked real (+2.7bp per 100bp of day move, t 1.9), but out-of-sample it reversed (-1.6, t -1.0). So there is no rule like "buy later on down days".

**First 15 minutes after the close (16:00 to 16:15):** this window contains none of the overnight gain. NVDL averages -2.6bp (t -0.83) and NVDX +0.2bp (t 0.08). This does not support entering before the close in order to catch the edge, and it does not support entering after the close either.

**Where the overnight return does come from (NVDL, 142 nights with every segment available):**

| Segment | bp |
|---|---|
| Close to 16:15 | -0.2 |
| 16:15 to 17:00 | +4.0 |
| 17:00 to 20:00 | +6.6 |
| 20:00 to 04:00 | +11.1 |
| 04:00 to 09:25 | +12.1 |
| 09:25 to exit | -2.3 |
| **Total** | **+30.9** |

The +0.77%/night post-market figure in RULES_v3 (from 25 nights) does not hold up over this longer sample.

**Net value at our size:** at about $85 invested (78% NVDL, 22% NVDX), the most favourable alternatives save very little. Entering at 15:59 saves about 2.5bp, or $0.02/night (90% CI -$0.09 to +$0.05). A 16:05 post-market limit order saves about 4.9bp gross, or $0.04/night. That is before the wider post-market spread, which takes back roughly half of it.

study.recommendation:
Keep the 15:52 entry and the §4 mechanics unchanged. Over 164 nights no other time from 15:30 to 16:15 is significantly cheaper.
- **Tests run:** 54 (9 candidate times × 2 symbols × 3 samples). The largest |t| is 1.54, below even the single-test 1.96 threshold; a Bonferroni correction for 9 times would need about 2.8.
- **What the 7-minute safety margin is worth:** a 15:59 marketable limit would have saved about 2.5bp on average, or about $0.02/night at $85 (90% CI -$0.09 to +$0.05). That is about $5 over 250 nights, with a CI of roughly ±$15.
- **What it would cost:** the 15:55 re-price and 15:58 cancel loop would go. A missed night costs the expected overnight edge, about 20 to 30bp or $0.17 to $0.26. So a 15:59 entry loses money on average if it fails to fill on more than about 10% of nights.
- **No reason to move into post-market:** the first 15 post-close minutes hold no edge (close to 16:15 is -2.6bp NVDL, +0.2bp NVDX). A 16:05 or 16:15 extended-hours limit order saves about 4 to 5bp gross (t about -0.8). An estimated extra 2 to 3bp of post-market half-spread takes back roughly half of that, NVDX fills are uncertain (it prints in only about 40% of post-market minutes), and the operational steps get more complicated.
- **Out-of-sample:** the Aug to Oct result (later entries 4 to 9bp cheaper) is not significant and is not seen in Feb to Jul, so do not act on it.
- **Optional, read-only:** at the §3(g) review, record NVDL/NVDX bid/ask quotes at 15:52, 15:59, 16:01, 16:05 and 16:15 for about 10 nights, to measure post-market spreads directly. Revisit entry timing only if a 15:52-to-close drift beyond ±10bp with t ≥ 2.5 shows up on at least 120 new nights.
caveats: The 5-minute proxies are not the exact 1-minute definitions. The 15:52 reference is OHLC4 of the 15:50-15:55 bar, about 2.9bp above the exact value (sd 17.6). Bar opens stand in for 15:30/15:45/15:50/15:55/16:05/16:15. On the 31 overlap nights the proxies agree with the exact 1-minute values: correlation 0.94 to 0.97 for 15:59 onward, but only 0.6 to 0.9 for 15:30 to 15:55, with level offsets of about 2 to 4bp.

The exit proxy (OHLC4 of the 09:30 5-minute bar) reads about +9 to +11bp above the exact 1-minute OHLC4(09:31) (sd about 40bp). The full-overnight levels in the tables are therefore overstated by roughly that much. The proxy is the same for every entry time, so it does not change the ranking.

Minute-level history is short. 5-minute bars exist only from 2026-02-23 and 1-minute bars only from 2026-09-08. There is no data from before 2026 or from other market regimes, and the overnight edge itself was about 0 in-sample (Feb to Jul) and about +54bp out-of-sample (Aug to Oct).

Spreads are not directly observed for any historical time. Regular-session spreads use the 1c quote (NVDL 33.66/33.67, NVDX 18.93/18.94 at 09:53 ET 10/21; same 1c in the journal on 10/13). Post-market spreads come from a Roll estimator on 1-minute trade prices (about 8bp), which is noisy, and real post-market quoted spreads could be wider.

Average post-market volume is about 900 shares/min for NVDL and about 500 shares/min for NVDX, against roughly 18,000 at 15:5x. Our 1 to 2 share orders are tiny, but whether NVDX fills after 16:00 is untested.

The 15:59 candidate assumes a marketable limit fills at the last-trade price. Robinhood has no market-on-close order. A 15:59 regular-hours order that has not filled by 16:00 would have to be handled (cancel or extended-hours) with no time to re-price, and closing-auction prices can move.
Multiple comparisons: 54 tests (9 times × 2 symbols × 3 samples), and the conditional rebalance test was added after the fact. Under a null of no effect, a few |t| values around 1.5 are expected.

No live entry fills exist for any time other than 15:52. Live calibration covers only the 15:52 entries (NVDL n=24, NVDX n=11), whose fills sit within about 1bp of OHLC4(15:52). Live exits vs OHLC4(09:31): NVDL +0.4bp (sd 30), NVDX +8.6bp (sd 37); the 10/16 and 10/19 open fades cost about 80bp on the re-priced exits.
Distribution ex-dates were not adjusted (split adjustment only). This affects overnight levels on those nights only, not differences between entry times.
The NVDA earnings blackout uses the verified pm report dates 2026-02-25, 2026-05-20 and 2026-08-26 for the nights tested; the next report is 2026-11-17.
study.spreads_bp: Regular session, measured: 1c quotes. On 10/21 at 09:53 ET NVDL was 33.66/33.67 (3.0bp) and NVDX 18.93/18.94 (5.3bp); the journal shows the same on 10/13. A marketable limit therefore pays about 1.5bp (NVDL) or 2.7bp (NVDX) half-spread. Live 15:52 fills vs 1-minute OHLC4(15:52) average -0.3bp NVDL (n=24, sd 7) and -1.1bp NVDX (n=11), so the realised regular-session entry cost is about 0 to 2bp at any time from 15:30 to 15:59. Post-market, estimated only: there are no historical quotes. A Roll estimator on 1-minute trade prices from 16:01 to 16:30 gives about 8.0bp effective spread for NVDL and 7.7bp for NVDX, i.e. about 4bp half-spread, or about +2 to 3bp per entry vs the regular session. NVDL trades in 79% of 16:01-16:05 minutes and 71% of 16:05-16:15 minutes (median about 600 to 900 shares/min vs 18k/min at 15:50-15:59). NVDX trades in only 43% and 36% (about 500 shares/min). Exit side at 09:31: live fills vs OHLC4(09:31) average +0.4bp NVDL (sd 30) and +8.6bp NVDX (sd 37). The 09:30 opening print sits about 20bp above OHLC4(09:31) (t -1.6, n=31), which is the open fade.
study.live_calibration: From trades.csv (read-only) against the 1-minute bars. NVDL 15:52 entries, 2026-09-09 to 10-20: fill minus OHLC4(15:52) = -0.3bp mean, +1.0 median, sd 7.0, n=24. NVDX: -1.1bp mean, sd 7.2, n=11. So the 15:52 OHLC4 reference is an unbiased stand-in for the real marketable-limit fill, within about ±1.5bp. Exits vs OHLC4(09:31): NVDL +0.4bp (sd 30, n=24) and NVDX +8.6bp (sd 37, n=11). On the faded-open nights the re-priced exits cost about -80bp: 10/16 entry exited 10/19 at 32.5714 vs OHLC4 32.84. On 10/14 the fill beat OHLC4 by 71bp. Entry slippage at 15:52 is small next to the ±30 to 60bp nightly noise in any entry-time difference, so no live evidence argues for another entry time.

issues: I could not refute the study. I rebuilt it from my own Robinhood pulls and my own parser (verify_entry/v_load.py and v_entry.py; none of the study's scripts or data reused). With the study's reference (OHLC4 of the 15:50 5-minute bar), every headline cell matched exactly: NVDL 15:59 -2.5bp (t -0.48), close -1.6 (t -0.32), 16:05 first trade -4.3 (t -0.72), 16:15 -4.2 (t -0.76); NVDX close -4.3 (t -0.82), 16:05 -5.3 (t -0.88, n=162). With a different reference (a Brownian-bridge estimate of the price at 15:52, o+0.4(c-o) inside the 15:50 bar) and different candidate prices (last trade before each time; post-market = OHLC4 of the 16:05 or 16:15 bar), every comparison stays within ±6bp. The largest |t| over all 164 nights is 1.06, so the conclusion does not depend on how the prices are defined.

Sample and timestamps check out. NVDA pm report dates confirmed with get_earnings_results: 2026-02-25, 05-20, 08-26 (next is 11-17). Intraday history really starts 2026-02-23: a 10-minute request for Dec 2025 returns only interpolated placeholder bars, so the 164 nights cannot be extended. Session labels line up on both sides of the 2026-03-08 DST switch (09:30 = 'reg', 16:00 = 'post'). Daily bars are 00:00Z-stamped and must be keyed by the UTC date; the study does this correctly (10/20 NVDL close 32.66 matches). Using bar-start timestamps (15:55 bar close = 15:59:59 last trade) is correct. I found no look-ahead.

Not reported by the study: the small 'later is cheaper' estimate comes almost entirely from 4 index-rebalance or expiry closes. On 3/20, 5/29 (MSCI), 6/26 (Russell) and 9/18 the 15:52-to-close moves were about +36, -355, -240 and +177bp, so the signs are mixed. Excluding those 4 nights, NVDL 15:52-to-close is -0.3bp (t -0.07, median +3.1) and NVDX -3.1bp (t -0.66). That leaves nothing systematic to trade on.

Not reported by the study: the 15:50 and 15:55 5-minute bars are about twice as volatile as earlier bars (rms open-to-close move 55 and 51bp vs 25 to 29bp; the closing-imbalance window). The 15:52 entry sits inside that window, which is why every late candidate has sd 65 to 78bp. Entering before the imbalance window, at 15:49-15:50, was not cheaper (+0.8 to +1.9bp, not significant).

A bias in the 5-minute reference that favours keeping 15:52. On the 31 nights with 1-minute data, both 5-minute references sit about 3bp (NVDL) and about 5bp (NVDX) above the exact 15:52 1-minute open (sd 16 to 19). Live fills are -0.2bp from that 15:52 open (sd 5.2, n=24) but -6.2bp (t -1.88) from the 5-minute bridge reference. So the 5-minute tables probably make every later entry look about 3bp cheaper than it really is, and the true saving is closer to zero than reported.

The 1-minute check reproduces the study's numbers (n=31): 15:59 -6.2 (t -0.57), close -5.6 (t -0.51), 16:05 -5.3 (t -0.43). The 15:50-to-15:52 move does not predict the 15:52-to-close move (correlation -0.12 NVDL, -0.01 NVDX; exploratory, n=31).

Power is low and the study does not say so. The 15:52-to-close difference has a standard error of about 5.3bp, so the smallest effect it could reliably detect is about 15bp. 'Not measurably worse' therefore cannot rule out a saving of 5 to 10bp ($0.04 to $0.09/night). The point estimate for the 78/22 basket is only -2.2 to -3.6bp ($0.02 to $0.03/night), and the proxy bias above probably accounts for most of that.

Minor overstatement: 'the largest |t| is 1.54, below the single-test 1.96 threshold' covers only the 54 entry-cost cells. The same study also reports the NVDX auction print vs the 15:59 last trade at t -2.0 (I get -1.7bp, t -2.02) and an in-sample rebalance slope with t 1.93 (I get 2.49, t 1.69). Both are economically trivial and do not change the conclusion. The 54 tests are also strongly correlated, since 15:59, close, 16:05 and 16:15 all contain the same 15:52-to-close move. Bonferroni is therefore conservative, but the conclusion is the same either way.

The breakeven fill-failure rate for a 15:59 entry rests on an overnight edge that is itself weak. My 15:52-to-09:30-open return is NVDL +20.2bp (t 1.03): in-sample -0.8, out-of-sample +61.9. If the true edge is about 10bp, the breakeven miss rate rises from about 10% to about 25%. That makes a 15:59 entry slightly less risky, but its gain is still not significant.

Post-market spreads are still unobserved; the Roll estimate (about 8bp) is the only number. It is 10:00 ET now, so I could not see a post-market quote, and the journal has no post-market bid/ask records. NVDX traded in the exact 16:05 bar on only 152 of 164 nights and in the 16:15 bar on 141, so post-market fill risk for NVDX is real.

Side claims confirmed. Post-market drift is small: NVDL close-to-19:55 is +6.0bp (n=159, t 0.68, median -2.5; in-sample -5.5, out-of-sample +28.2), so RULES_v3's +0.77%/night post-market figure does not hold up. Close-to-16:15 is -2.0bp (t -0.63). The conditional rebalance slope reverses between halves (in-sample +2.49, t 1.69; out-of-sample -1.34, t -0.85). Live exits vs 1-minute OHLC4(09:31) are NVDL +0.2bp (n=23, sd 31) and NVDX +9.5bp (n=10, sd 39); the 10/19 fade exits cost -82 and -79bp.

Hygiene: I made no orders and no repo writes; only read-only Robinhood calls (historicals, earnings). git status shows trader/journal.md modified, but that change is not mine; it is presumably the live agent's own logging. Scratch is in verify_entry/: v_ingest.py, v_load.py, v_entry.py, v_vol.py, v_m1.py and v_extra.py, with outputs v_entry_out.txt/.json, v_vol_out.txt, v_m1_out.txt and v_extra_out.txt, and raw pulls in raw/.

verdict.adjusted_recommendation:
Adopt: keep the 15:52 entry and the §4 mechanics unchanged, as the study says. My independent rebuild matches its numbers exactly. On a different reference choice no time from 15:30 to 16:15 is significantly cheaper (|t| at most 1.06 over 164 nights; |t| at most 0.6 on the 31 exact 1-minute nights).

The small point estimate in favour of later entry (basket about 2 to 4bp, or $0.02 to $0.03/night) has three problems:
- It comes almost entirely from 4 index-rebalance or expiry closes with mixed signs. Without them NVDL is -0.3bp.
- It is probably inflated by about 3bp because the 5-minute reference sits high. Live fills sit within 0.2bp of the exact 15:52 price.
- It would cost the 15:55 re-price and 15:58 cancel safety loop, and add fill risk (no market-on-close order on Robinhood; NVDX is thin in post-market).

Two wording fixes to the study:
- State the power limit: the smallest reliably detectable effect is about 15bp, so effects of 5 to 10bp cannot be ruled out.
- Note that two of its side tests reached |t| of about 2 (NVDX auction print, in-sample rebalance slope), even though none of the entry-time cells did.

Nothing to defer except the optional read-only logging of post-market quotes (15:59, 16:05, 16:15) at the §3(g) 40-night review, because post-market spreads have never been observed. Reopen entry timing only on the study's own pre-registered bar: at least 120 new nights, with the 15:52-to-close drift beyond ±10bp and t of at least 2.5. Do not reopen it on the Aug–Oct split.
verdict.confidence: High that the study's numbers and its null conclusion are right. They reproduce exactly with independent code, and a different reference moves estimates by only about 1bp. Medium on the post-market cost side, because post-market spreads have never been observed (Roll estimate only), though any error there only strengthens keeping 15:52. Main limits: only 164 nights, all in Feb–Oct 2026 (no earlier intraday history exists on this server), and only 31 nights of exact 1-minute data.
